### Clarendon County

- **Type:** County
- **Recorded status:** 🟢 Active
- **Date enacted:** September 14, 2026 (County Council third and final reading and public hearing, per WIS; second reading was at an Aug. 24, 2026 special called meeting, first reading Aug. 10, 2026)
- **Normalized date:** `2026-09-14` (exact)
- **Duration:** Six months
- **Current end date:** `—`
- **Sectors:** data center, battery storage
- **Moratorium ID:** `sc-clarendon-county-2026`
- **Legal basis:** Ordinance 2026-18 (Clarendon County Council)
- **What prompted it:** County's Unified Development Code does not specifically define data centers or battery energy storage systems; council sought to close a loophole after learning of a proposed "Project 59" data center in the county industrial park, and to give time to set standards for setbacks, buffers, noise, lighting, and emergency access.
- **Affected projects:** Proposed "Project 59" data center in the county industrial park (Santee Electric Cooperative / developer identified as "Five Nines"); this project is not paused by the moratorium because it is sited in an Industrial I district.
- **Detailed status:** Active as of 2026-09-23; adopted unanimously on third and final reading Sept. 14, 2026, following a public hearing. Pauses land-use and development approvals for data centers and battery storage facilities outside areas zoned Industrial I or Industrial II; does not affect the proposed Project 59 data center, which is sited in an Industrial I district and received a conditional-use determination from county planning staff.
- **Outcome:** Adopted six-month moratorium on data center and battery energy storage system approvals outside industrially zoned areas.

### H. 4583 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `sc-h-4583-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Reps. Cromer et al.; R lead (Cromer is SC House Republican) [VERIFY: complete cosponsor party-by-party tally not extracted into this profile]
- **Recorded status:** Prefiled 2025-12-16; introduced and read first time 2026-01-13; referred to House Labor, Commerce and Industry Committee; sponsors White, Reese, Lawson, and Atkinson added between 2026-01-20 and 2026-02-18; no committee vote or further action as of 2026-07-31
- **Provisions:** "South Carolina Data Center Responsibility Act." Requires complete energy independence, bars state and local taxpayer-funded incentives, requires closed-loop water or liquid cooling with zero net water withdrawal and discharge, imposes strict liability and insurance/bonding, and sets employment/reporting requirements.
- **Mechanism / scope:** incentive_restriction; fiscal
- **Legal effect:** proposed
- **Effective date:** —
- **End condition and limitations:** —
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess126_2025-2026/bills/4583.htm>)

### H. 5286 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `sc-h-5286-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Reps. Steven Long et al.; R lead (Long is SC House Republican); full cosponsor list shows mostly Republicans on the SC General Assembly bill page [VERIFY: complete cosponsor party-by-party tally not extracted into this profile]
- **Recorded status:** Introduced and read first time 2026-02-26; referred to House Ways and Means Committee; sponsors Hager and Gilliam removed 2026-03-05 and 2026-03-31; no committee vote or further action as of 2026-07-31
- **Provisions:** Statewide moratorium joint resolution. Would prohibit state, county, municipal, and political-subdivision final approval for new data center applications, permits, rezoning, special exceptions, special use permits, building permits, site plans, plans of development, FILOTs, and incentives until 2028-01-01. Defines data center at 1 MW or more.

- **End condition and limitations:** 2028-01-01
- **Primary reference:** [Official source](<https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess126_2025-2026/bills/5286.htm>)

### H. 5526 (2026)

- **Policy ID:** `sc-h-5526-2026`
- **Sponsor / party:** Rep. J.L. Johnson; D
